clusters.name: Building with steel for GCs
clusters.summary: Help general contractors evaluate residential steel, prepare their crews and manage a project with Wheeler framing.
clusters.purpose: The GC introduction is scheduled October 8, crew preparation October 12 and first-job readiness October 19. Later articles cover finish coordination, panelized-project integration and resource tracking.
jobs: Decide whether adding project-specific residential steel framing is a suitable option for the GC’s work.
Prepare a wood-framing crew to understand the material-specific knowledge required for cold-formed steel.
Confirm the actual project is ready for framing delivery and crew assembly.
Understand how the chosen framing material affects dimensional consistency and coordination of finished surfaces.
Explain the roles and information needed when custom framing complements a panelized approach.
Track framing resource use during the job so delivery, waste and cleanup performance can be evaluated consistently.

jobs: Explain the differences between material, off-site preparation and whole-home delivery methods.
Provide a supplier-fit comparison matrix tied to an actual residential design.
Explain what each credential establishes and how to verify the relevant party.

clusters.name: Wildfire rebuild framing decisions
clusters.summary: Help rebuilding homeowners evaluate framing within a whole-home resilience plan and understand the project team and property designation process.
clusters.purpose: Four articles cover framing choice, a whole-home planning checklist, rebuild-team roles and the IBHS designation roadmap. Existing Pacific Palisades and fire-resilience pages remain relevant destinations.
audiences: Southern California homeowners rebuilding after wildfire
jobs: Explain the material and planning factors that shape a rebuild framing decision.
Record the whole-home resilience decisions and evidence a homeowner’s rebuild team must coordinate alongside the steel framing.
Plan and complete the whole-property measures needed for an IBHS Wildfire Prepared Home designation.
Explain which party leads each design, supply and construction responsibility.

clusters.name: Quote and cost evaluation
clusters.summary: Help owners and builders evaluate complete costs, quotation terms, reported project comparisons and insurance information.
clusters.purpose: Five financial articles and three insurance articles have distinct tasks. IBHS designation, material stability and resource tracking are placed in the clusters matching their reader purpose.
jobs: Normalize two or more actual framing proposals for the same approved home design.
Compare the initial installed framing budget for equivalent engineered wood and steel designs.
Understand published California wildfire discount opportunities and calculate the premium component to which they apply.
Explain the insurance stage and covered-property categories relevant during construction.
Build a transparent post-occupancy cost comparison using the owner’s estimates and dated property-specific quotations.
Understand how the stated commercial terms of one framing proposal determine the price boundary and later adjustments.
Compare actual completed-home insurance quotations for the same property with different approved construction descriptions.
Interpret Wheeler’s three reported residential dollar-savings examples by keeping each project and comparison baseline separate.
